CHIEF COMPLAINT
Right leg pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mrs. Peterson is a 43-year-old female who presents with right leg pain after a bowling injury. She reports that while bowling, she was running up to the lane with her bowling ball pulled back and slung it forward, striking her right leg instead of the lane. She fell at the time of injury. She reports no significant swelling but does have some bruising on the back of the leg. She is able to walk only a little bit and only very carefully. Walking is very sore. She states she would avoid stairs at all costs. On physical examination, there is significant tenderness to the lateral aspect of the right upper leg. No pain or tenderness is noted with flexion or extension of the lower leg.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Not discussed.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Atopic eczema.
Colectomy for diverticulosis and diverticulitis.

MEDICATIONS
Fluocinonide for eczema, used as needed when itchy.
Ibuprofen and Tylenol, alternating for current leg pain.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Not discussed.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Significant tenderness to the lateral aspect of right upper leg. No pain or tenderness with flexion or extension of lower leg.

RESULTS
X-ray of right femur: normal femur, no evidence of fracture or swelling.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Contusion of right upper leg. Start mobic 15 mg once daily as an anti-inflammatory. Use ice for pain management. Patient counseled that symptoms should improve within one week. Patient instructed to return if not improving.
